sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球供应链制造母港、跨境电商货源地与外资合规准入市场

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Refrigerated Logistics Warehousing for Perishable Pharmaceuticals

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Mainland China (People's Republic of China) with Hong Kong SAR as the investing conduit jurisdiction
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Mainland and Hong Kong Closer Economic Partnership Arrangement (CEPA, 2003, as supplemented)
Investment Agreement under the Mainland and Hong Kong Closer Economic Partnership Arrangement (signed 28 June 2017)

Arrangement between the Mainland of China and the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with respect to Taxes on Income (1998, as amended by the 2019 Protocol)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Partnership Enterprise Law of the PRC (2006, as amended 2019); Foreign Investment Law of the PRC (2019, effective 1 January 2020); Anti-Money Laundering Law of the PRC (2024 Revision, effective 1 January 2025); Administrative Measures for the Registration of Beneficial Owner Information (PBOC and SAMR Order No. 3, effective 1 November 2024); Measures for the Administration of the Registration of Foreign-Invested Partnership Enterprises (SAMR/SAIC 2010); and applicable PBOC financial institution AML/CFT regulations.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation / Partnership Registration Certificate of the Foreign-Invested Partnership
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: State Administration for Market Regulation / Municipal Market Regulation Administration of the PRC
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarize at the issuing registry notary. If origin is a Hague Apostille Convention state, obtain an Apostille from the competent authority and submit directly to the Chinese receiving office. If origin is not an Apostille state, obtain Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication and then consular legalization at a PRC embassy or consulate. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive; never chain them.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Current Status Certificate of the Hong Kong investing partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarize at a Hong Kong notary public. For mainland China receipt, apply through Hong Kong High Court Apostille if the registration office accepts the Hague route, or obtain notarisation and authentication through China Legal Services (Hong Kong) Limited where required; alternatively, authenticate with the Hong Kong SAR Department of Justice and legalise at the Commissioner's Office of the PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Hong Kong. Do not combine Apostille with consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolutions and Power of Attorney of the Investing Entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the Hong Kong investing entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certify the resolutions by the company secretary and director; notarize at a Hong Kong notary. If the destination authority applies the Hague Apostille Convention, obtain an Apostille from the Hong Kong High Court. If consular legalization is required, obtain High Court authentication and then consular legalization at a PRC consular post. The two paths are parallel; never chain them sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association / Partnership Agreement of the Foreign-Invested Partnership
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Founding partners of the Foreign-Invested Partnership
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Execute in Chinese and English before a notary public in the place of signing; for a foreign partner's signature, notarize the signature at a qualified notary and then obtain either an Apostille if the signatory state is a Hague member or consular legalization if non-member. Use only one authentication route.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for KYC and Creditworthiness
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing commercial bank in Hong Kong or Mainland China
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Issue on bank letterhead with an authorised officer's signature and bank seal; notarize the banker's signature if the document will cross jurisdictions. Obtain an Apostille from the competent authority if the bank is located in an Apostille state; if not, arrange consular legalization at a PRC embassy or consulate. Apostille and consular legalization are alternative, non-concurrent procedures.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Conduct mandatory screening of every general partner, limited partner, UBO, authorised representative and bank signatory against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN and Non-SDN Lists, EU and UK consolidated financial sanctions lists, PRC MOFCOM sanctions and unreliable entity list, HK CEPS sanctions list, and SAMR/PBOC adverse identification databases. Screen all domestic and foreign politically exposed persons (PEPs) using risk-tiered verification; obtain source-of-wealth documentation, senior management approval, and enhanced continuous monitoring for any PEP match. Escalate all hits to the China Anti-Money Laundering Monitoring and Analysis Center and file a suspicious transaction report within statutory deadlines before any incorporation step proceeds. Re-run screening every 30 days during formation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: PRC National Enterprise Name Registration and Self-Service Declaration System administered by the State Administration for Market Regulation, accessible through the China Integrated Government Service Platform and local Municipal Market Regulation Administration online systems.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered name must use simplified Chinese characters. The four-tier statutory sequence is administrative division, distinctive trade name, industry or business characteristics such as refrigerated logistics or cold-chain warehousing, and organizational form such as Limited Partnership Enterprise or General Partnership Enterprise. The English name is auxiliary and must be transliterated in Pinyin unless a licensed international brand name is used; the Chinese name is authoritative for registration and licensing.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Limited Partnerships Ordinance (Cap. 37), sections 4, 5, 6, and 7; Partnership Ordinance (Cap. 352), sections 3 and 4; Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310), section 6; Pharmacy and Poisons Ordinance (Cap. 138) and Pharmacy and Poisons Regulations (Cap. 138A); Dangerous Goods Ordinance (Cap. 295); Occupational Safety and Health Ordinance (Cap. 509)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies Registry, 14/F, Queensway Government Offices, 66 Queensway, Hong Kong; and Inland Revenue Department, Business Registration Office, 4/F, Revenue Tower, 5 Gloucester Road, Wan Chai, Hong Kong
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form LP1 (Application for Registration of a Limited Partnership) filed with the Companies Registry; Form IRBR 1 (Application for Registration of Business) filed with the Inland Revenue Department Business Registration Office
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. Hong Kong law imposes no minimum paid-up capital requirement and no blocked escrow account rule for a Foreign-Invested Limited Partnership. The amount and form of capital contributions are determined solely by the Partnership Agreement, and all contributions may be in cash or in-kind as agreed by the partners.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [•] FOREIGN-INVESTED PARTNERSHIP (THE 'PARTNERSHIP'), ADOPTED BY WRITTEN CONSENT OF THE GENERAL PARTNER IN LIEU OF A MEETING ON [DATE]. WHEREAS the Partnership is to be formed as a limited liability partnership under the Limited Partnerships Ordinance (Cap. 37) and the Partnership Ordinance (Cap. 352) of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region; WHEREAS the following resolutions are necessary and proper for the formation, registration, capitalization, and licensing of the Partnership and each resolution shall be deemed effective as of the date of this consent; NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, as follows: 1. CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION: That the Partnership shall commence with the capital subscription of HK$[•] or such other amount as the General Partner shall determine, and the partners are authorized to contribute cash or in-kind assets as set out in the Partnership Agreement. No capital shall be returned or distributed except in accordance with the Partnership Agreement and applicable law. 2. REGISTERED OFFICE: That the registered office and principal place of business of the Partnership in Hong Kong shall be at [•], and the General Partner is authorized to execute such lease, consent to use, or other documents as may be required by the Companies Registry or the Inland Revenue Department. 3. OFFICER APPOINTMENTS: That [•] is appointed as General Partner, [•] is appointed as the authorized representative for service of process, and [•] is appointed as the statutory records officer charged with maintaining the partnership books, accounts, registers, and minutes at the registered office. 4. BANKING AUTHORIZATION: That the General Partner is authorized to open, operate, and close one or more bank accounts at any licensed bank in Hong Kong, and the following persons are appointed as authorized signatories: [•]. For any transaction exceeding HK$[•], the signature of any two authorized signatories shall be required unless otherwise instructed by the General Partner. 5. LICENSING AND REGULATORY FILINGS: That the authorized officers are directed to file Form LP1 and Form IRBR 1, to obtain the Business Registration Certificate, and to apply for all permits, licenses, and approvals required for the operation of a temperature-controlled cold storage and refrigerated logistics warehouse under the laws of Hong Kong, including but not limited to the Pharmacy and Poisons Ordinance, the Dangerous Goods Ordinance, and the Occupational Safety and Health Ordinance. 6. INDEMNIFICATION AND CONCLUSION: That all acts previously taken by the partners in connection with the formation and financing of the Partnership are ratified and approved, and no further consent of any partner is required for the payment of formation fees, government fees, legal fees, and notarial charges. RESOLVED FURTHER, that any officer or partner is hereby severally authorized to sign, execute, affix the seal if any, deliver, and file all documents, certificates, applications, returns, and instruments of every kind required to carry out these resolutions and to cause the Partnership to commence lawful business immediately. This resolution shall continue in full force and effect until revoked in writing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-registration Name Search and Partnership Structure Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry, Hong Kong SAR; online name search through e-Registry (www.eregistry.gov.hk)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name search using the Companies Registry electronic name search facility to ascertain that the proposed English and Chinese name is not identical or too similar to an existing registered business. Prepare the draft Partnership Agreement and capital contribution schedule. If a partner is a foreign corporation, obtain a good standing certificate and a resolution nominating a representative. The General Partner must certify that the proposed name includes the word Partnership or Limited Partnership as appropriate and does not include restricted words such as Bank or Trust. Execute the registered office address consent and landlord authorization. Retain certified English translations for all non-English documents. This step does not require notarization unless the relevant government office requests a certified translator declaration.
required_dossiers: Proposed English and Chinese partnership name
Draft Partnership Agreement
Identity documents of all general and limited partners
Certificate of incorporation and good standing for corporate partners
Registered office address commitment and landlord consent
Capital contribution schedule
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is rejected for similarity, submit an alternative name immediately. If identity documents are queried, provide certified English translations, apostilled or notarized originals, or a solicitor certification within seven working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of the Limited Partnership with the Companies Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry, Registry of Limited Partnerships, Hong Kong SAR; e-Registry portal for submissions
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form LP1, being the application for registration of a limited partnership, and have it signed by the general partner. Submit Form LP1 together with the original partnership agreement or a certified copy to the Companies Registry, either in person or through the e-Registry. Attach notarized or solicitor-certified copies of the passports or identity cards of all general and limited partners, certificate of incorporation and registered office records for corporate partners, and the landlord consent for the registered office. Pay the prescribed registration fee and receive the Certificate of Registration of Limited Partnership. If any document is not in English, attach a certified English translation. The certificate should be checked for name, date and partner details before acceptance.
required_dossiers: Form LP1 signed by the general partner
Original or certified copy of the Partnership Agreement
Certified true copies of identity documents of all partners
Certificate of incorporation, business registration certificate, and director list of corporate general partner
Landlord consent and proof of registered office address
Prescribed government fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a query or suspension, file a written response within fourteen calendar days. Amend the Partnership Agreement or Form LP1 as requested, pay any additional fee, and resubmit. If the deadline cannot be met, apply in writing for an extension and provide a timeline for corrected documentation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration with the Inland Revenue Department
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department, Business Registration Office, Hong Kong SAR; eTAX portal at www.etax.gov.hk
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month of the date upon which the partnership begins business, submit Form IRBR 1 to the Inland Revenue Department Business Registration Office. Attach the Certificate of Registration of Limited Partnership and proof of the principal place of business. The Department will issue a Business Registration Certificate upon payment of the applicable business registration fee and levy. The same filing serves as registration under the Business Registration Ordinance for tax purposes; a separate tax registration certificate is not required. For a pass-through partnership, the Business Registration Certificate is essential for opening bank accounts and applying for operating licenses. Retain the certificate at the registered office and display a copy at the business premises at all times.
required_dossiers: Form IRBR 1 duly completed
Certificate of Registration of Limited Partnership
Proof of registered office and principal place of business
Identity document copies of partners
Business registration fee and levy
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried for missing information, provide the requested particulars within seven days. If late registration is alleged, submit a written explanation and evidence of the actual commencement date; apply for a penalty waiver or mitigation in writing to the Business Registration Office.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Industrial and Physical Licensing for Temperature-Controlled Cold Storage and Pharmaceutical Logistics
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Health, Pharmacy and Poisons Office; Fire Services Department; Buildings Department; Environmental Protection Department; Labour Department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before operating the temperature-controlled cold storage, file an application with the Department of Health for a Wholesale Dealer Licence under the Pharmacy and Poisons Regulations if the warehouse will store pharmaceutical products, and with the Fire Services Department for a Certificate of Fire Service Installations and Equipment. Submit architectural and engineering drawings certified by an authorized person and a registered structural engineer, temperature validation and mapping protocol, standard operating procedures, refrigeration unit specifications, and a dangerous goods inventory. If ammonia or other dangerous refrigerant is stored, apply for a Dangerous Goods Licence under the Dangerous Goods Ordinance. Provide the Environmental Protection Department with an environmental exemption brief; only if the facility is deemed a designated project will an environmental permit be required. Obtain an Occupation Permit from the Buildings Department and fire load assessment approval before stocking any perishable pharmaceuticals.
required_dossiers: Site floor plan and building Occupation Permit
Temperature validation, mapping, and IQ/OQ/PQ reports
Standard operating procedures for storage, quarantine, and dispatch
Certificate of Fire Service Installations and Equipment
Dangerous Goods Licence application and inventory, where applicable
Refrigeration contractor license and equipment certification
Environmental exemption letter or environmental permit, as applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Department of Health queries the Wholesale Dealer Licence application, submit amended validation data and SOPs within fourteen working days. If the Fire Services Department requires additional fire containment, appoint a registered fire services contractor, remedy the non-compliance, and submit the updated certificate. If the Environmental Protection Department rejects the exemption classification, prepare a full environmental impact assessment report or environmental permit application within thirty days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Activation, Statutory Records, and Post-Registration Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed bank in Hong Kong; Companies Registry and Inland Revenue Department for post-registration filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registry and licensing approvals, open a bank account with a licensed bank using the partnership incorporation and licensing documents. Complete the bank anti-money laundering and know-your-client forms, provide declarations of source of funds and beneficial ownership, and execute a bank mandate jointly with the General Partner. After account opening, maintain the statutory register, partnership records, minutes, and temperature compliance logs at the registered office. Notify the Companies Registry and Inland Revenue Department of any change in partners or principal place of business using Form LP2 and Form IRBR 2, respectively. File Profits Tax returns on behalf of the partnership and ensure business registration certificates and operating licenses are renewed annually.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Registration of Limited Partnership
Business Registration Certificate
Partnership Agreement and First Board Resolution
Bank KYC and AML forms with beneficial ownership declarations
Source of funds and source of wealth evidence
Proof of registered office address and specimen signatures
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests additional enhanced due diligence, provide notarized identity documents, certified financial statements, and a written explanation of the commercial purpose. If funds cannot be verified, consider an alternative licensed bank or multi-bank arrangement. If a post-registration filing is rejected by the Companies Registry or Inland Revenue Department, file a correction or objection within fourteen days and pay the prescribed late fee if applicable.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Department of Health, Pharmacy and Poisons Office; Fire Services Department; Buildings Department; Environmental Protection Department; Labour Department of the Hong Kong SAR
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Wholesale Dealer Licence under the Pharmacy and Poisons Regulations (Cap. 138A); Dangerous Goods Licence under the Dangerous Goods Ordinance (Cap. 295); Certificate of Fire Service Installations and Equipment under the Fire Services Ordinance (Cap. 95); Occupation Permit and structural safety certificate from the Buildings Department; Business Registration Certificate under the Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Department, Hong Kong SAR
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from a full EIA report under the Environmental Impact Assessment Ordinance (Cap. 499) for standard warehousing and cold storage that is not a Schedule 2 or Schedule 3 designated project; an environmental permit and registration will only be required if the Director of Environmental Protection determines that the facility is a designated project by reason of scale, location, or adjacent sensitive uses.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No EIA-specific quantitative thresholds apply to a non-designated standard cold storage facility. However, any trade effluent discharged to a foul sewer must comply with licence conditions under the Water Pollution Control Ordinance (Cap. 358), including generally pH 6-10, BOD5 not exceeding 300 mg/L, COD not exceeding 500 mg/L, and suspended solids not exceeding 350 mg/L. Air emissions must not cause noxious or offensive odours under the Air Pollution Control Ordinance (Cap. 311). Ammonia refrigeration systems must be fitted with certified pressure vessels, leak detection, and containment systems, and refrigerants must comply with the Ozone Layer Protection Ordinance (Cap. 403) phase-out schedules for CFCs and HCFCs.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Services Department Certificate of Fire Service Installations and Equipment and Fire Safety Certificate under the Fire Services Ordinance (Cap. 95); Buildings Department Occupation Permit and structural load inspection certificate for racking and mezzanine floors; Labour Department safety inspection and compliance with the Occupational Safety and Health Ordinance (Cap. 509) and the Factories and Industrial Undertakings Ordinance (Cap. 59); mandatory certified temperature alarm systems, emergency lighting, fire extinguishing systems, and workplace safety approval for ammonia and refrigerant risk management.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD), Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, including the Business Registration Office (BRO); electronic portal: eTAX at https://www.etax.gov.hk. The Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310) is administered by the IRD.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Apply to the Business Registration Office under the Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310) within one month of commencing business in Hong Kong, using the statutory application for business registration (Form IRBR1). Step 2: The IRD issues a Business Registration Certificate (BRC) containing the Business Registration Number (BRN); the BRN is the sole statutory tax identification number for the Foreign-Invested Partnership (FIP). Step 3: If the FIP is constituted as a limited partnership, it must also be registered with the Companies Registry under the Limited Partnerships Ordinance (Cap. 37) using the prescribed statement of particulars; the Limited Partnership Certificate does not replace the BRN. Step 4: No separate VAT identification number exists in Hong Kong because Hong Kong has no VAT/GST. Each foreign non-resident partner is assessed directly on the allocated share of partnership profits under the Inland Revenue Ordinance (Cap. 112), and the IRD may issue tax returns or assessments directly to a non-resident partner having assessable profits sourced in Hong Kong.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible; for Hong Kong Profits Tax purposes the FIP is transparent. The partnership itself is not taxed as a separate entity; partners are chargeable on their respective shares of the partnership profit under sections 22, 22A and 25A of the Inland Revenue Ordinance (Cap. 112), with territorial sourcing rules applying to each partner.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Hong Kong has no check-the-box or hybrid mismatch entity classification election. Partnership treatment is mandatory under the Inland Revenue Ordinance, and no election is available to change the pass-through characterization. Advance rulings may be requested from the IRD on specific transactions, but such rulings are not entity classification elections.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: No general VAT, GST, or sales and use tax in Hong Kong; Hong Kong levies only targeted indirect duties such as those under the Dutiable Commodities Ordinance (Cap. 109) and the Hotel Accommodation Tax Ordinance (Cap. 348).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Not applicable; Hong Kong has no VAT/GST and accordingly no monetary threshold triggering indirect tax registration. However, every business, including an FIP carrying on business in Hong Kong, must obtain a Business Registration Certificate under the Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310) irrespective of turnover.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory electronic invoicing, real-time fiscal clearance, API-based reporting, or anti-fraud digital stamping regime exists in Hong Kong. Taxpayers must instead preserve sufficient business records for at least seven years under section 51C of the Inland Revenue Ordinance (Cap. 112).

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Not applicable; Hong Kong does not operate a VAT or GST, so there is no export zero-rating election and no statutory mechanism for claiming a 0% VAT export rate. Exported goods and cross-border services from Hong Kong are outside the scope of indirect taxation. For Profits Tax purposes, an FIP in the refrigerated logistics warehousing sector may argue that certain income is not sourced in Hong Kong and thus not taxable, but that is a territorial profits tax analysis rather than an export VAT zero-rating claim.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Not applicable for VAT zero-rating: no Hong Kong export VAT declaration or VAT zero-rating substantiation bundle is required.

To support any offshore-source Profits Tax argument, retain contracts, invoices, purchase orders, warehouse receipts, temperature logs, customs export documents, bills of lading or airway bills, courier receipts, and communications evidencing where the refrigerated logistics services are performed and where the customer or recipient is located.

To evidence foreign exchange repatriation for group risk management, retain bank credit advisories, SWIFT messages, and settlement statements; Hong Kong maintains no foreign exchange control requirement or statutory repatriation deadline for export proceeds.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Not applicable: no VAT or GST zero-rating is claimed, so there is no VAT clawback or export-fraud penalty in Hong Kong. However, if an FIP or partner makes an incorrect Profits Tax treatment of Hong Kong-sourced income as offshore-source income, the IRD may raise estimated assessments, impose penalties of up to three times the amount of tax undercharged under section 82A of the Inland Revenue Ordinance (Cap. 112), and in serious cases pursue criminal prosecution. The anti-avoidance rules in sections 61 and 61A may also disregard artificial transactions entered into solely for tax avoidance.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBoC) and State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE); Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) acts as the de facto central bank for the Hong Kong SAR leg where no FX controls exist.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Chinese FIP is domiciled in the People's Republic of China and therefore falls under SAFE's foreign-exchange control framework. The RMB is fully convertible on the current account (trade in goods/services, dividends and royalties) after genuine business documents and tax receipts are presented to a designated bank, but the capital account remains heavily regulated. Foreign capital contributed to a Foreign-Invested Partnership must flow through a designated FDI capital settlement account, and the original currency (usually USD or HKD) may be converted to RMB only after the bank has verified the subscription agreement, SAFE FDI registration, paid-in capital certificate and business scope compliance. Profit remittance to foreign partners is permitted but requires a copy of the audited annual financial statements, the board/partner resolution approving distribution, and the corporate income tax withholding voucher; banks may freeze remittance if the partnership is not in good standing with the State Administration of Taxation. There is no mandatory surrender of export proceeds for current account receipts since the 2012 reform, but all export earnings must be repatriated to China within the prescribed timeline and retained in a designated foreign currency account or voluntarily converted into RMB. Immediate conversion for capital injections is not automatic; a capital account FX conversion form must be lodged with the bank, and the proceeds cannot be used for working capital beyond the registered scope. Any profit deemed earned from impermissible activities or unreported ultimate beneficiaries will trigger AML review and potential SAFE penalties.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: China abolished mandatory surrender percentages for current account export proceeds; enterprises may retain all foreign currency receipts in a settlement account or convert to RMB at their discretion. Export proceeds must be repatriated to the domiciled bank and go through trade credit verification within 180 days from the date of export customs declaration (extendable to 360 days with a valid SAFE reason). Receipts for pre-shipment on account must be registered as advance receipts and unreleased within 30 days after delivery. Failure to repatriate within the timeline is an administrative violation under the Foreign Exchange Control Regulations (Regulations of the People's Republic of China on Foreign Exchange Control, 2008).

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of China Limited (Shanghai Branch or the branch local to the FIP's registered address)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: FDI Capital Settlement Account (foreign currency capital account) & RMB Basic Operational Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited (ICBC)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (for temporary capital custody) + General Settlement Account (RMB)
Operational Currency Account (CNY & HKD) for trade settlements

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMIs (e.g., Wise, Airwallex, Revolut Business) are not licensed by the PBOC/CBIRC to maintain domestic current or capital accounts for a Chinese Foreign-Invested Partnership, and they cannot undertake SAFE foreign-exchange registration or capital verification. They may be used solely as ancillary cross-border payment channels for inbound disbursements after a licensed commercial bank has opened a sponsor bank account, but they are legally barred from acting as the primary account provider or holding the entity's capital injection. For a cold storage logistics FIP needing full bank guarantees, trade finance and SAFE compliance, a Tier-1 onshore bank is mandatory. Any EMI that cannot provide a China bank branch with a full KYC relationship should be rejected for the main treasury function.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a mainland-registered FIP, the managing partner (or a China-resident deputy with a notarized power of attorney) must physically appear at the bank counter in Mainland China for the initial signing of account documents and the KYC interview. Remote consular proxy opening is not recognized by Chinese banks. If the statutory foreign partner is offshore (e.g., a Hong Kong entity), its ultimate beneficial owners and authorized signatory must submit notarized certificates of incumbency, Hong Kong business/CR registration, and, when required, attend a video-conference KYC call with a mainland branch officer while physically being in Hong Kong. This hybrid physical-video protocol is the standard accepted method for foreign-invested partnerships today.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Partnership ownership opacity where a Hong Kong or offshore entity as general partner creates red flags on ultimate beneficial ownership (UBO).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A full ownership chain chart, certified English/Chinese translations of partnership agreements, Hong Kong Business Registration Certificate and Annual Return, certified register of members and UBO declarations (CAP 622 compliant), notarized passports of beneficial owners, plus a written explanation of each partner’s economic substance in Hong Kong or China.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection whose source-of-funds documents are inconsistent with the expected net worth of the foreign investor.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Twelve to twenty-four months of audited bank statements for the remitting entity and its beneficial owners, certified dividend/distribution vouchers, sale-and-purchase contracts for any matched assets, tax assessments showing after-tax profitability, and a formal letter of comfort from an international commercial bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and PEP exposure of the ultimate partners, particularly where a moderate-risk jurisdiction like Hong Kong is viewed as a conduit for third-country funds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Negative-hit screening reports from a reputable global database, self-declaration of PEP status, government-issued consent letters or sanctions waiver documents if applicable, and a copy of the Hong Kong registered office’s latest fee invoices and local payroll records to prove substantive presence (not a shell).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business scope mismatch between the stated cold-storage warehouse activity and the partnership’s lack of a required pharma storage licence or physical facility.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A bank-verified warehouse inspection report, refrigerated facility lease/residential title deeds, temperature-monitoring logs for 12 recent months, the FIP’s statutory operational license (e.g., drug storage distribution license or food logistics permit), and signed client contracts with pharmaceutical companies proving genuine trade.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For the Chinese FIP, the foreign partner must first ensure the partnership is registered with the Market Regulation Authority and the foreign investment information report is filed. The bank then completes SAFE's FDI (Foreign Direct Investment) registration for the partnership and opens a fiduciary 'FDI Capital Settlement Account' in the same currency as the contribution. The investor remits via SWIFT MT103 with the beneficiary bank being the designated onshore branch, using the BOP transaction purpose code from the SAFE 6220 series (Foreign direct investment inflows – capital contribution) and the correct custody line 'FDI CAPITAL SETTLEMENT ACCOUNT'. Bank officers will perform capital verification against the signed partnership agreement; only after the capital has landed and the bank has issued a paid-in certificate may the partnership convert the funds into RMB (or use a 'payment before settlement' priority for designated expenditures) and transfer the RMB to its operational current account for permitted cold-storage operating expenses. Any deviation from the registered use (e.g., investing into brokerage or offshore lending) triggers a SAFE penalty.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound payments are cleared through the onshore branch using SWIFT MT103 for ordinary current-account trade (e.g., shipping refrigerated containers, maintenance parts from overseas vendors) supported by an invoice, contract and customs declaration where applicable. For recurring purchases of expensive compressors, insulation panels or bonded linings from overseas suppliers, a commercial Letter of Credit (MT700) issued by the Bank of China or ICBC with a 90-day sight tenor gives the partnership secure deferred settlement and better payment terms. Documentary Collections (MT400/MT540) can be used for low-risk, out-of-warranty spare parts that do not require title documents. All trade outflows must align with the 5210 cold-storage logistics scope; a mismatch in the goods description is an AML red flag.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable CNY/USD FX forward contracts (with a physical delivery to the designated settlement bank) under a real current-account exposure documentary file for procurement of cold-storage equipment and international electricity/fuel tariffs.
Cross-currency swaps (CCS) to convert syndicated USD/HKD equipment-lease liabilities into RMB payment streams, provided the underlying loan has completed SAFE foreign-debt registration.

FX options (vanilla purchase only) and zero-cost collars (two-bank simultaneous call/put) for protection against adverse translation of future capital contributions or dividend absorptions, clearly tied to verified committed flows. Offshore NDFs are not permissible for an onshore FIP without SAFE approval; therefore NDF contracts are excluded from this hedging blueprint.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Business Registration Certificate Renewal and annual Business Registration Fee receipt
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department - Business Registration Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before the expiry date shown on the current Business Registration Certificate; IRD ordinarily issues a renewal demand notice one month before expiry and no statutory grace period is available after expiry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal attracts an additional statutory penalty of HK$300; continuing to carry on business without a valid Business Registration Certificate is an offence under the Business Registration Ordinance punishable by a maximum fine of HK$5,000 and imprisonment for up to one year, and the IRD may prosecute or commence automatic estimated assessments

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profits Tax Return for Partnership (BIR52) with certified tax computation and supporting partnership accounts when requested
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department - Assessor of Profits Tax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days from the date of issue shown on the BIR52; for standard financial years ending 31 December or 31 March, the IRD normally publishes extended due dates under its annual tax return filing practice
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file without reasonable excuse is an offence under the Inland Revenue Ordinance; the maximum penalty is HK$10,000 plus a further daily default fine, the assessor may raise estimated profits tax assessments, and where tax is undercharged the court may impose additional tax of up to 300% of the undercharged tax

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Employer's Return of Remuneration and Pensions (BIR56A) together with individual IR56B forms
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department - Employer Returns Unit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within one month of the date of issue of BIR56A; for a year of assessment ending 31 March, the IRD generally requires filing in early May unless an extension is published
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or inaccurate filing is an offence under the Inland Revenue Ordinance carrying a maximum fine of HK$10,000 and, on continued default, daily penalties; the IRD may also impose estimated employer assessments and initiate prosecution

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual renewal of the Wholesale Dealer in Medicines / cold-chain pharmaceutical storage licence
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Department of Health - Drug Office / Pharmacy and Poisons Board
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually before the expiry date stated on the licence; the renewal application must be submitted in advance of expiry, as a matter of pharmacy licensing practice, at least 60 days before the current licence expires
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Operating a refrigerated pharmaceutical warehouse without a valid licence is unlawful under the Pharmacy and Poisons Ordinance; the Board may suspend or refuse renewal, continued operation without a licence attracts fines of up to HK$100,000 and imprisonment for two years on indictment, and any lapsed licence terminates lawfully approved drug storage premises

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Limited Partnership Annual Confirmation / Updated Statement of Particulars (Form LP2 or prescribed equivalent) where the Foreign-Invested Partnership is registered as a limited partnership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 14 days of any change in the registered particulars, including changes to partners, capital contributions, business nature, principal place of business, or general partner details; an annual confirmation, where prescribed, is aligned to the anniversary of registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to lodge the prescribed statement is an offence under the Limited Partnerships Ordinance; the maximum fine is HK$5,000 with a daily default fine, and persistent non-compliance may lead to deregistration or strike-off action by the Registrar

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Hong Kong Partnership Ordinance and Limited Partnerships Ordinance, no statutory audit is imposed on a pure Foreign-Invested Partnership solely by reference to turnover, total assets, or employee headcount. A certified independent audit by a qualified CPA becomes legally mandatory where: (a) the partnership agreement, investor side letter, or banking covenant requires an audited statement; (b) the Inland Revenue Department requires an auditor's report in support of the Profits Tax Return where accounts are material or unresolved; (c) the Department of Health / Pharmacy and Poisons Board imposes an audited financial statement condition for renewal of the Wholesale Dealer in Medicines licence; (d) the same business is carried on through a Hong Kong company under Cap. 622, in which case qualified auditor appointment is required unless the company is dormant or a valid members' dispensation applies; or (e) the partnership is consolidated into an offshore parent's statutory audit. No numerical audit threshold exists for a Hong Kong partnership vehicle itself.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Hong Kong Financial Reporting Standards (HKFRS), which are fully converged with IFRS for all true and fair view reporting; eligible small-and-medium-sized entities may apply HKFRS for Private Entities / Hong Kong SME-FRS; tax computations must be reconciled to assessable profits under the Inland Revenue Ordinance (Cap. 112); if the partnership is consolidated into a PRC parent, PRC GAAP may additionally apply for group reporting but the Hong Kong statutory books remain on the elected HK reporting framework.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Hong Kong does not maintain a public beneficial-ownership register for partnerships. The Foreign-Invested Partnership must nonetheless maintain and continuously update internal beneficial-ownership records under the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance (Cap. 615), conduct customer due diligence and ongoing monitoring of all partners, and file any transfer of a partnership interest or change in limited partner particulars with the Companies Registry within 14 days. If the entity is ever required to be treated as a Hong Kong company or registered non-HK company, the Significant Controllers Register must be kept at the registered office and updated within 7 days of any change in significant controllers; a prescribed annual confirmation is then required under the Companies Ordinance with penalties for non-maintenance.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 450 - USD 1,500 per annum for registered office, licensed corporate service provider, and compliance agent fees
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500 - USD 12,000 per engagement depending on partnership complexity, cold-chain inventory verification, licensing support, and consolidation requirements

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 15% non-corporate standard profits tax (FIP assessed at partner level; corporate partners assessable at 16.5%); two-tiered relief: first HK$2,000,000 of profits at 7.5% (non-corporate)/8.25% (corporate), excess at 15%/16.5%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday. Effective reliefs: (i) territorial source exemption for offshore-sourced active income; (ii) 100% first-year-initial capital allowance of 60% plus annual allowances of 10%-30% on refrigeration plant and machinery; (iii) 300%/200% super-deduction for eligible R&D expenditure (first HK$2M/balance); (iv) full deduction for qualifying cold-chain facility renovation costs per IRD depreciation tables.
